finding.claim: Decode errors for individual form properties are silently discarded when decoding application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies. A property whose value fails to parse (for example a non-integer in an integer field) is dropped from the decoded object instead of rejecting the request. Schema validation then runs on an object without that field, so an optional typed property is never validated. The original raw body is still forwarded to the handler.
finding.source: HTTP request body with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded, e.g. 'limit=abc' or 'flag=<payload>' for an optional integer/boolean property
finding.sink: decodeSchemaConstructs `if err != nil || !present { continue }` leads to ValidateRequestBody VisitJSON on an object that lacks the malformed property, which returns nil. The unmodified request body then reaches the downstream handler.

trace.note: ValidateRequestBody calls decodeBody on the attacker-supplied body
decodeProperty error is ignored with `continue`, so the property is omitted from obj
Schema validation passes on the object without the property
Body is only rewritten when defaults were applied, so otherwise the original raw bytes are restored to req.Body and passed on

finding.guards_checked: The urlencoded decoder returns early for object-typed properties and arrays of non-primitive items (lines 1426-1448). The `parameter.Required` check applies only to parameters, not to body properties. A schema `required` list would still catch a missing property, but optional properties get no check. In contrast, query parameters that fail to decode return an error (ValidateParameter lines 181-183 and 224-227). No other control enforces type on the dropped property.
